## Problem

The Thailand wave (S212) stopped silently with 19 tours stuck `ingested`; it took a manual count to notice, and the first count was wrong. The wave report rule (S209: S1 ok / to Master / to review + reason / atomized) is right but done by hand. Jev fails open, so call counts are not evidence that Jev ran.

## Scope

1. A wave record with `expected_set` (tour ids) written before the run.
2. A wave ends only when every tour is in a terminal state: `master`, `review_pending`, `trashed`, `failed`, `interrupted`.
3. Endpoint generates the 4-column report + failure reasons/class, Jev coverage % (tours with a real Jev verdict / total), LLM + DFS cost of the wave.
4. Alert when `expected ≠ tours in a terminal state` after the wave's jobs finish.

## Done when

The Laos wave report is generated by the endpoint and matches a manual count.

Source: Harness Engineering → AA-CIS doc, sections 3.5 and 5.3 — [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7052bb82-54ea-4f4d-9a5f-79a58d29cea2](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7052bb82-54ea-4f4d-9a5f-79a58d29cea2>)
